text:
maya: Heads up — rethinking billing windows + sessionized cache crediting. Prototype in the console is showing negative savings for some short sessions (looks like credits assigned to the wrong tenant). Anyone run into this?

alex: Hmm can you paste repro steps or a quick trace? I haven't seen negatives before.

maya: repro: 1) start session A -> many cache hits 2) session A crosses a billing boundary (midnight or window cut) 3) subsequent requests routed via fallback lane and cache credits jump to tenant B. Seems like we bind credits to routing epoch instead of session owner.

sam: That sounds like the usual race between session tagging and late routing resolution. We had similar with quota counters. Quick fix is to sticky-bind billing_window_id at session start. Minimum billing window also helps.

tariq: What's the user-visible harm? Is this only a dashboard artifact or actual charge shift?

maya: For now mostly dashboard noise — but can affect per-model/unit economics when we aggregate by tenant for monthly invoices. Short-lived sessions (<30s) are the worst.

alex: Can we add a pending-credit row in the dashboard UX so that credits that haven't been reconciled show as "pending" and don't flip the unit-econ view? Helps finance not freak out.

sam: Agreed. Also prefer a config flag: `min_billing_window_secs` default 30s. If session < min then flush credits into the pool and reconcile later. Keeps invoices deterministic.

maya: Putting a small example of what I'm seeing in logs:
```
173d: session_start id=abc123 tenant=team-x
173d+10s: cache_hit session=abc123 model=redwood-7B
173d+28s: billing_window_cut window=2024-04-04T23:59:00Z
173d+35s: routed -> fallback_tenant=team-y (cache credits applied to team-y)
```

alex: Ugh. For telemetry we should add these tags to every request emit: `billing_window_id`, `session_owner`, `route_decision_ts`, `cache_hit`. Then we can join later and attribute correctly.

maya: Exactly. Proposed immediate plan: (1) sticky billing_window_id at session start for attribution (2) emit per-request tags for post-join reconciliation (3) UX: show pending credits and a small note about settlement lag (4) add `min_billing_window_secs` default 30s for short sessions.

tariq: On routing side, watch out for sticky-routing TTLs. If we keep session->route affinity too long it can hurt load balancing. Make sure billing sticky != routing sticky.

sam: Also callout: quantization/mini-batches can distort token counts for short sessions (batched requests get token counts merged). Telemetry should capture `token_count_raw` vs `token_count_batched`.

maya: Good point. I'll open an RFC and include sample telemetry schema + dashboard mock. Will also add a small canary rollout on dev env with `min_billing_window_secs=30`.

alex: If you want I can mock the pending line in the console quickly — a small sparklines + "pending credits" with hover explanation.

maya: Please do. Link to RFC when done: <https://tiny.redwood/rfc/session-billing-windows> (wip).

deploy-bot: deploy: feature/session-billing-window default flag toggled on staging — build 20240404.2 — tests passed :white_check_mark:

sam: Awesome. After staging canary, let's run a 24h reconciliation job and compare invoice deltas before enabling in prod.

maya: Agreed. I'll kick off a compare job and post results here. Thanks all :rocket:
